final_answer:
Let a point of \(K\) be written as
\[
(m_1,m_2,m_3,m_4)=\int_0^1 (t,t^2,t^3,t^4)\,d\mu(t)
\]
for a probability measure \(\mu\) on \([0,1]\). Thus \(K\) is the moment space of order \(4\) on \([0,1]\).

Set
\[
x=m_1,\qquad y=m_2,\qquad z=m_3,\qquad w=m_4.
\]

For fixed \(x\), the possible \(y\) satisfy
\[
x^2\le y\le x.
\]
Write
\[
y=x^2+x(1-x)q,\qquad 0\le q\le 1.
\]
For fixed \(x,y\), the possible \(z\) satisfy
\[
\frac{y^2}{x}\le z\le y-\frac{(x-y)^2}{1-x}.
\]
The width of this interval is
\[
y-\frac{(x-y)^2}{1-x}-\frac{y^2}{x}
=x(1-x)q(1-q).
\]
So write
\[
z=\frac{y^2}{x}+x(1-x)q(1-q)r,\qquad 0\le r\le 1.
\]

For fixed \(x,y,z\), the fourth moment \(w\) has lower and upper bounds coming from the nonnegativity of
\[
\int (t^2-at-b)^2\,d\mu(t)
\]
and
\[
\int t(1-t)(t-c)^2\,d\mu(t).
\]
These give
\[
w_{\min}=\frac{y^3-2xyz+z^2}{y-x^2},
\qquad
w_{\max}=z-\frac{(y-z)^2}{x-y}.
\]
Substituting the above parametrization for \(y,z\), their difference simplifies to
\[
w_{\max}-w_{\min}
=x(1-x)q(1-q)r(1-r).
\]
Thus write
\[
w=w_{\min}+x(1-x)q(1-q)r(1-r)s,\qquad 0\le s\le 1.
\]

The map \((x,q,r,s)\mapsto(m_1,m_2,m_3,m_4)\) is triangular, so its Jacobian is
\[
1\cdot x(1-x)\cdot x(1-x)q(1-q)\cdot x(1-x)q(1-q)r(1-r).
\]
Hence
\[
J=x^3(1-x)^3q^2(1-q)^2r(1-r).
\]

Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_4(K)
=\int_0^1\int_0^1\int_0^1\int_0^1
x^3(1-x)^3q^2(1-q)^2r(1-r)\,ds\,dr\,dq\,dx.
\]
Compute:
\[
\int_0^1 x^3(1-x)^3\,dx=\frac1{140},
\]
\[
\int_0^1 q^2(1-q)^2\,dq=\frac1{30},
\]
\[
\int_0^1 r(1-r)\,dr=\frac16,
\]
and \(\int_0^1 ds=1\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{Vol}_4(K)=\frac1{140}\cdot\frac1{30}\cdot\frac16
=\frac1{25200}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{25200}}
\]
